items.new: Stubb was the second mate. He was a native of Cape Cod, and so, according to local usage, was called a Cape-Cod-man. A happy-go-lucky type; neither cowardly nor valiant; taking dangers as they came with an indifferent air; and in the most urgent crisis of the chase, toiling away, calm and collected as a journeyman joiner hired for the year. Good-humored, easy, and carefree, he presided over his whale-boat as if the deadliest encounter were only a dinner, and his crew all invited guests. He was as particular about the comfortable arrangement of his part of the boat as an old stagecoach driver is about the snugness of his seat. When close to the whale, in the very death-lock of the fight, he handled his pitiless lance coolly and offhandedly, as a whistling tinker handles his hammer. He would hum his old rigadig tunes while flank to flank with the most furious monster. Long habit had, for this Stubb, turned the jaws of death into an easy chair. What he thought of death itself, there is no telling. Whether he ever thought of it at all might be a question; but if he ever did happen to turn his mind that way after a comfortable dinner, no doubt, like a good sailor, he took it to be a sort of call of the watch, summoning the men on watch to tumble aloft and get busy there about something he would find out when he obeyed the order, and not sooner.

items.new: Soon after his first appearance on deck, he withdrew to his cabin. But after that morning, he was visible to the crew every day — either standing in his pivot-hole, or sitting on an ivory stool he had, or walking heavily across the deck. As the sky grew less gloomy and even began to turn a little mild, he became less and less of a recluse, as if, when the ship first sailed from home, nothing but the dead winter bleakness of the sea had kept him shut away. Gradually, he was almost constantly in the open air. But for all he said or visibly did on the deck, sunny at last, he seemed as unnecessary there as an extra mast. The Pequod was only making a passage, not actively cruising. The mates were fully capable of handling nearly all the whaling preparations that needed overseeing. So there was little or nothing outside of himself to occupy or excite Ahab now, and so to chase away, for that one interval, the clouds that were piled layer upon layer on his brow — just as all clouds always choose the loftiest peaks to pile themselves upon.

items.new: "I never had such a queer dream, King-Post. You know the old man's ivory leg? Well, I dreamed he kicked me with it; and when I tried to kick back, upon my soul, my little man, I kicked my leg right off! And then, presto! Ahab seemed to be a pyramid, and I, like a blazing fool, kept kicking at it. But what was still more curious, Flask — you know how curious all dreams are — through all this rage I was in, I somehow seemed to be thinking to myself that, after all, it wasn't much of an insult, that kick from Ahab. 'Why,' thinks I, 'what's the row? It's not a real leg, only a false leg.' And there's a mighty difference between a living thump and a dead thump. That's what makes a blow from the hand, Flask, fifty times more savage to bear than a blow from a cane. The living limb — that's what makes the living insult, my little man. And all the while, mind you, I was thinking to myself, while I was stubbing my silly toes against that cursed pyramid — so confoundedly contradictory was it all — all the while, I say, I was thinking to myself, 'What's his leg now but a cane — a whalebone cane? Yes,' thinks I, 'it was only a playful cudgeling — in fact, only a whaleboning he gave me — not a low kick. Besides,' thinks I, 'just look at it: why, the end of it — the foot part — what a small sort of end it is; whereas if a broad-footed farmer kicked me, now there's a devilish broad insult. But this insult is whittled down to a point only.' But now comes the biggest joke of the dream, Flask. While I was battering away at the pyramid, a sort of badger-haired old merman with a hump on his back takes me by the shoulders and swings me round. 'What are you up to?' says he. Lord! man, but I was frightened. Such a mug! But somehow, the next moment I was over the fright. 'What am I up to?' says I at last. 'And what business is that of yours, I'd like to know, Mr. Humpback? Do you want a kick?' By the Lord, Flask, no sooner had I said that than he turned his stern to me, bent over, and, dragging up a lot of seaweed he wore for a loincloth — what do you think I saw? — why, thunder alive, man, his stern was stuck full of marlinspikes, with the points out. Says I, on second thought, 'I guess I won't kick you, old fellow.' 'Wise Stubb,' said he, 'wise Stubb,' and kept muttering it all the time, a sort of chewing on his own gums like an old hag by the chimney. Seeing he wasn't going to stop saying over his 'wise Stubb, wise Stubb,' I thought I might as well go back to kicking the pyramid. But I had only just lifted my foot for it when he roared out, 'Stop that kicking!' 'Hello,' says I, 'what's the matter now, old fellow?' 'Look here,' says he; 'let's argue the insult. Captain Ahab kicked you, didn't he?' 'Yes, he did,' says I — 'right here it was.' 'Very good,' says he — 'he used his ivory leg, didn't he?' 'Yes, he did,' says I. 'Well then,' says he, 'wise Stubb, what have you got to complain of? Didn't he kick with right good will? It wasn't a common pitch-pine leg he kicked with, was it? No, you were kicked by a great man, and with a beautiful ivory leg, Stubb. It's an honor; I consider it an honor. Listen, wise Stubb. In old England the greatest lords think it a great glory to be slapped by a queen and made Knights of the Garter; but let your boast be, Stubb, that you were kicked by old Ahab and made a wise man of. Remember what I say: be kicked by him; count his kicks as honors; and on no account kick back; for you can't help yourself, wise Stubb. Don't you see that pyramid?' With that, all of a sudden, he seemed somehow, in some queer fashion, to swim off into the air. I snored, rolled over, and there I was in my hammock! Now, what do you think of that dream, Flask?"
